purpose: Define source-driven saint title and qualifier rendering by locale and ecclesial context. Never translate or mechanically transform saint titles across languages.

canonicalStatusAndCauseIdentity: Dicastery for the Causes of Saints (causesanti.va)
liturgicalDisplayName: official local/national liturgical authority for the target locale and tradition
Holy See official liturgical source in the target language
Dicastery for the Causes of Saints
secondaryUsageEvidence: reputable explanatory press and religious media

contexts.calendarCompact: Use the abbreviation or compact form explicitly validated for that locale/tradition.
contexts.saintPageTitle: Use the full official liturgical/hagiographic display form for the target locale.
contexts.runningText: Follow grammar and capitalization rules of the target language; do not force title-case conventions from headings.
contexts.institutionOrPlaceName: Treat as a proper name; do not reuse person-name morphology rules blindly.

examples: São Gregório Magno, papa e doutor da Igreja
Santa Maria Goretti, virgem e mártir

papalAndHistoricalNames.ordinalPolicy: Never infer, add or remove a Roman numeral. Preserve the exact official target-locale liturgical or Holy See form.
papalAndHistoricalNames.epithetPolicy: Prefer the official liturgical epithet when that is the established saint display name.

primaryAuthorities: Dicastery for the Causes of Saints

personPrefixRule.capitalization: In ordinary prose, language authorities normally lowercase san/santo/santa when used as treatments; official liturgical headings may use their own heading capitalization. Preserve source context.
Preserve the official liturgical context. French liturgical calendars may use 'S.' in compact headings and 'saint/sainte' in running text.

examples: S. Grégoire le Grand, pape et docteur de l'Eglise

personPrefixRule.policy: Do not abbreviate automatically. Use the form selected by the target ecclesial/style authority for the context.

examples: Saint Gregory the Great, Pope and Doctor of the Church
primaryAuthorities: local Catholic bishops' conference / approved liturgical source

personPrefixRule.policy: Do not translate Saint/São mechanically. Preserve validated German ecclesial usage such as 'hl.'/'Heiliger' according to source and context; 'St.'/'Sankt' is commonly part of institutions, churches and place names and is not interchangeable with person labels.

primaryAuthorities: German Catholic liturgical authority / bishops' conference

personPrefixRule.policy: Preserve official Polish ecclesial form (commonly św. in compact liturgical usage and inflected full forms in running text). Do not generate forms without case-aware source validation.

primaryAuthorities: Polish Episcopal Conference / approved Polish liturgical source

personPrefixRule.policy: Preserve official Russian ecclesial form and grammatical case (e.g. святой/святая and inflected forms). Never transliterate when a validated Cyrillic form exists.
Preserve the official Filipino Catholic form from an approved local ecclesial source. Do not infer Spanish, English or Portuguese saint prefixes.

primaryAuthorities: Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines / approved Filipino liturgical source

personPrefixRule.compact: Mt. / Wat. only when explicitly validated by the local liturgical source

primaryAuthorities: Tanzania Episcopal Conference / diocesan approved liturgical sources
